title: Tau-induced mitochondrial reverse electron transport drives neurodegeneration
title_zh: Tau 诱导的线粒体反向电子传递驱动神经退行性变
abstract: Hyperphosphorylation and aggregation of tau are pathological hallmarks of tauopathies. Mitochondrial dysfunction is also a common feature of tauopathies. The mechanistic link between tau abnormalities and mitochondrial dysfunction and its relationship to the physiological function of tau, however, is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that tau regulates mitochondrial reverse electron transport (RET), which produces excess reactive oxygen species (ROS), reduces the NAD+/NADH ratio, and is activated by aging or stress. In flies, mice, and human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neurons, tau depletion eliminates stress-induced RET and confers resilience. Mechanistically, tau enters mitochondria and directly interacts with the complex I subunit NDUFS3 to promote RET in a phosphorylation-dependent manner. Elevated RET further drives tau hyperphosphorylation, establishing a self-perpetuating pathological loop. Inhibition of RET ameliorates tau toxicity across species. RET regulation thus represents a previously unrecognized normal function of tau that becomes pathological in disease, providing a therapeutic target for various conditions characterized by tau abnormalities and mitochondrial dysfunction.
abstract_zh: Tau 过度磷酸化和聚集是 tau 蛋白病的病理标志，线粒体功能障碍也十分常见，但二者的机制联系及其与 tau 生理功能的关系不清楚。研究证明，tau 可调控线粒体反向电子传递（RET）；该过程在衰老或应激时激活，产生过量活性氧并降低 NAD+/NADH 比值。在果蝇、小鼠和人诱导多能干细胞来源神经元中，去除 tau 可消除应激诱导的 RET 并提高抗性。机制上，tau 进入线粒体并与复合体 I 亚基 NDUFS3 直接相互作用，以磷酸化依赖方式促进 RET。升高的 RET 又推动 tau 过度磷酸化，形成自我维持的病理循环。抑制 RET 可在多个物种中减轻 tau 毒性。RET 调控由此被识别为 tau 此前未知的正常功能，在疾病中转为病理过程，并可成为多类 tau 异常和线粒体功能障碍疾病的治疗靶点。
